items.title: Salah agrees two-year Trabzonspor deal — Reports
items.description: Former Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah has reportedly reached an agreement to join Turkish Super Lig side Trabzonspor on a two-year contract. According to FootballTransfers, Turkish transfer journalist Yagiz Sabuncuoglu claimed the Egyptian star has agreed personal terms with the club, although the deal is yet to be finalised. The report added that one contractual clause still requires approval before the transfer can be officially completed. Salah has been a free agent since leaving Liverpool earlier this summer, ending a remarkable nine-year spell at Anfield in which he established himself as one of the Premier League’s greatest players. The 34-year-old had previously been linked with a move to the Saudi Pro League, while MLS clubs San Diego and Sporting Kansas City were also reported to be interested. However, recent reports suggest the Egyptian prefers to remain in European football. Trabzonspor, who finished third in the Turkish Super Lig last season, have been active in the transfer market and are preparing for their UEFA Europa League playoff later this month. Despite the latest reports, uncertainty still surrounds the move. Just days earlier, Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan dismissed reports claiming the club had already reached an agreement with Salah. As speculation over his next destination continues, Mohamed Salah was seen unwinding at a beach club in Psarrou, Mykonos, in footage published by Mykonos Live TV on August 4. The Egyptian star has been without a club since his Liverpool deal expired earlier this summer, with reports claiming three clubs from two countries are still awaiting his decision. items.title: Clerics, presidency clash over economy after Tinubu-bishops meeting
items.description: By Olayinka Latona A meeting between President Bola Tinubu and the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) has sparked public debate over the role of religious leaders in governance, with differing opinions emerging on whether clerics should openly comment on government policies or remain focused on spiritual matters. The debate intensified after Cardinal John Onaiyekan granted a television interview in which he shared his perspective on the meeting, drawing reactions from the Presidency, religious leaders, political commentators and members of the public. Cleric urges prayer, caution Pastor Seyi Osuntayo, Area Superintendent of The Apostolic Church Nigeria, Igbein Area, said the exchange between the Presidency and the Catholic bishops was unfortunate. He observed that while religious leaders have a role in national discourse, the timing of public criticism could influence how such comments are perceived. “The timing of advice and criticism is important. The timing of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria’s comments could be interpreted differently by various audiences,” he said. Osuntayo maintained that Christian leaders should avoid partisan political disputes and instead encourage good governance while continuing to pray for national leaders. Quoting 1 Timothy 2:1-4, he said Christians are instructed to pray for those in authority regardless of political differences. “Our leaders need prayer, whether we agree with their leadership style or not. We may not choose our leaders, but we can choose to obey God’s instruction to pray for them,” he said. He also cautioned against what he described as the increasing involvement of some religious leaders in political debates through media engagements, arguing that prayer should remain central to the Church’s response to governance issues. Commentator faults Presidency’s response Journalist and author Ben Charles-Davies said attention should remain on the concerns raised by the bishops rather than the controversy surrounding their comments. According to him, issues such as poverty, insecurity and the cost of living deserve greater public attention. Charles-Davies noted that the Catholic Bishops had also criticised previous administrations, including that of former President Goodluck Jonathan, arguing that religious leaders have consistently commented on governance regardless of the government in power. He said public officials should respect differing opinions and avoid personal attacks on critics. He further argued that Cardinal Onaiyekan’s remarks reflected concerns widely expressed by many Nigerians over insecurity, inflation and the rising cost of living. ‘President owes no political allegiance to bishops’ Speaker, author and entrepreneur Ugoji Maximillian offered a different perspective, describing the Catholic bishops as an influential institution with a long history of engagement in national affairs. He argued that disagreements between political leaders and religious groups are not unusual in Nigeria’s democratic process. Maximillian expressed the view that the bishops had previously taken positions during the 2023 general elections which, in his opinion, influenced current perceptions of their relationship with the Tinubu administration. He also said President Tinubu appeared committed to implementing his economic agenda despite criticism from various quarters. Ayinde urges patience with reforms Former Lagos State Commissioner for Physical Planning, Toyin Ayinde, said economic reforms often require time before their full impact becomes evident. He argued that Nigerians should evaluate ongoing reforms over the long term rather than expecting immediate results. Ayinde cited his personal experience using a naira debit card for international transactions as an example of changes within Nigeria’s financial system. He also called for constructive engagement on national issues, urging stakeholders to contribute ideas that could help improve governance. Presidency defends administration In a statement, Presidential media aide Temitope Ajayi defended the administration’s handling of the economy and responded to Cardinal Onaiyekan’s comments. Ajayi said the bishops had requested the meeting with the President and were given the opportunity to present their concerns on economic, social and security issues. He argued that while the bishops acknowledged the impact of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), they did not sufficiently recognise other achievements of the administration. According to him, President Tinubu inherited significant fiscal challenges and has implemented reforms aimed at stabilising the economy. Ajayi cited improved salary and pension payments in several states as evidence of progress under the current administration. He also addressed the bishops’ request for the return of mission schools, stating that the matter falls within the constitutional responsibilities of state governments. According to him, President Tinubu reminded the bishops that he returned mission schools to their original owners during his tenure as Governor of Lagos State. Ongoing national conversation The differing reactions to the meeting have reignited debate over the role of religious leaders in public affairs. While some believe clerics have a responsibility to speak on issues affecting citizens, others argue that their primary role should be spiritual guidance and prayer. The exchanges also underscore broader discussions about economic reforms, governance and the relationship between religious institutions and political leadership in Nigeria. items.title: GNAPS calls for transparent standards-based BECE grading instead of norm-referenced assessment
items.description: The General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Private Schools (GNAPS), Justice King Essiel, has questioned the transparency of the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) grading system, arguing that the continued use of norm-referenced assessment is inconsistent with Ghana’s current education reforms. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, August 4, Mr Essiel said the existing grading model ranks candidates against one another rather than measuring them against fixed performance standards, making it difficult for parents, teachers and schools to determine students’ actual academic achievement. He explained that Ghana’s assessment system was originally designed when progression to higher levels of education was highly competitive, with only the best-performing students advancing through stages such as the Common Entrance Examination and the O-Level system. However, he noted that educational reforms “have become compulsory, and every child is expected to move on to the next level. But while the system has changed, the assessment method has largely remained the same,” he said. According to him, under the current norm-referenced grading system, candidates are ranked against their peers instead of being assessed against predetermined performance benchmarks. “They are comparing children with other cohorts. So, for example, even if a student scores 80 marks, that student may not receive Grade One if the score does not place them within the top-performing group,” he explained. Mr Essiel argued that because only grades are released and not candidates’ raw scores, parents and schools are unable to accurately assess students’ actual performance. He called for a standards-based grading system similar to that used at the senior high school level, where grade boundaries are clearly defined. “We expect that if Grade One is awarded for scores between 75 and 100, then that should be made clear. If the quality of education is declining, stakeholders should be able to identify it and work together to improve it,” he added. Mr Essiel maintained that greater transparency in the grading process would strengthen confidence in the examination system and provide educators with more meaningful data to evaluate learning outcomes.

items.title: Rogbanè : un complexe balnéaire de 42 millions de dollars annoncé par le ministère de la Culture
items.description: Le ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat a annoncé, ce mardi 4 août, la signature d’une convention de partenariat avec l’entreprise sino-guinéenne Sino-Gui pour transformer la plage de Rogbanè, à Ratoma, en un complexe balnéaire moderne. Le projet, évalué à 42 millions de dollars, sera réalisé sur environ 15 hectares dans le cadre d’un partenariat de 20 ans. La plage de Rogbanè pourrait bientôt changer de visage. Le ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat a conclu, ce mardi à Conakry, un accord avec Sino-Gui pour l’aménagement et la valorisation de ce site du littoral. Porté par un investissement privé annoncé à 42 millions de dollars, le projet prévoit la construction d’un important complexe consacré au tourisme, aux loisirs et aux activités balnéaires. Sur une superficie d’environ 15 hectares, le futur site devrait comprendre des hôtels de haut standing, une marina, un complexe cinématographique, un parc aquatique, des espaces sportifs et de loisirs, un marché maritime, un parking intelligent ainsi qu’une promenade aménagée. Les promoteurs tablent sur une fréquentation comprise entre 2 000 et 7 000 visiteurs par semaine. Pour le ministère de la Culture, ce projet s’inscrit dans la dynamique de Simandou 2040, qui vise notamment à développer les infrastructures touristiques et à créer de nouvelles opportunités économiques à travers le pays. Des retombées attendues pour les Guinéens Le partenariat doit également favoriser la création d’emplois, le développement des entreprises locales et le renforcement des compétences nationales. Le chef de cabinet du ministère, Baba Thiam, cité par le Service de Communication du Ministère, a expliqué que la convention repose notamment sur la mobilisation de l’investissement privé et le respect des procédures prévues dans le cadre des partenariats public-privé. Il a également mis en avant l’assistance à la maîtrise d’ouvrage, qui doit se traduire par des actions de formation et un appui en équipements. Autre particularité annoncée : la commune de Ratoma devrait bénéficier d’une part des recettes générées par l’exploitation du site. De son côté, le ministre de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Moussa Moïse Sylla, a insisté sur la nécessité de faire de ce projet un levier de développement du contenu local et de transfert de compétences. Au-delà de sa vocation touristique, le site de Rogbanè porte une forte charge mémorielle. Le 29 juillet 2014, une bousculade sur cette plage avait fait 34 morts. Une tragédie qui reste gravée dans la mémoire collective. Moussa Moïse Sylla souhaite donc que la transformation du site s’accompagne d’un devoir de mémoire. Le ministre a notamment évoqué l’installation d’une stèle en hommage aux victimes. « Nous comptons sur vous pour faire un travail sérieux sur ce site », a-t-il lancé à l’endroit des promoteurs, en insistant sur le respect des engagements contractuels, des délais et des normes de construction. items.title: Gaza : les médiateurs dénoncent les frappes israéliennes et redoutent l’échec du cessez-le-feu
items.description: Le 3 août, le Qatar, l'egypte et la Turquie ont exprime, dans une declaration commune, leur vive inquietude face a la poursuite des operations militaires israeliennes dans la bande de Gaza. Les trois pays, qui jouent un role central dans les efforts de mediation entre Israel et le Hamas, estiment que ces frappes compromettent la mise en œuvre de la prochaine phase du cessez-le-feu et menacent les recents progres diplomatiques. Les mediateurs accusent Israel de violer le droit international et le droit international humanitaire, affirmant que plusieurs frappes ont vise des infrastructures medicales et provoque de nombreuses victimes civiles, notamment parmi les femmes et les enfants. Selon eux, ces operations sont incompatibles avec les engagements prevus dans la feuille de route de paix, alors que le Hamas a accepte le plan presente par les mediateurs, y compris la disposition relative au confinement de ses armes. Une pression inutile ? Doha, Le Caire et Ankara estiment que la poursuite des hostilites risque d'aneantir les efforts de desescalade engages ces dernieres semaines et d'aggraver encore la crise humanitaire dans l'enclave palestinienne. Ils rappellent que la deuxieme phase du cessez-le-feu repose sur le respect des engagements pris par l'ensemble des parties. Les trois capitales appellent egalement Israel a respecter ses obligations internationales, a garantir la protection des civils, des etablissements de sante et des travailleurs humanitaires, ainsi qu'a assurer la continuite de l'acheminement de l'aide humanitaire et medicale vers Gaza. Enfin, les mediateurs exhortent la communaute internationale a accroître la pression diplomatique sur Israel afin de permettre la mise en œuvre du plan de paix presente par le president americain Donald Trump, qu'ils considerent comme la meilleure base actuelle pour parvenir a une desescalade durable et relancer le processus politique.

items.title: Tinubu hails Team Nigeria’s performance at Commonwealth games
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — ​PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has congratulated Team Nigeria on their remarkable performance at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland. ​The President celebrated the athletes for demonstrating the resilience, determination, discipline, and excellence that define the Nigerian spirit. ​President Tinubu according to the statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, commended Team Nigeria for flying the country’s flag with dignity and pride, affirming that the 24 medals won—10 gold, 7 silver, and 7 bronze—are a testament to their hard work and perseverance. ​The President noted that the experience gained by every athlete will serve as a strong foundation for greater accomplishments in future international competitions and inspire many young Nigerians to embrace the values of commitment and national service. He ​praised the leadership of the Nigeria Olympic Committee and the National Sports Commission for their continued commitment to the development of sports and support for athletes. ​The President urged the athletes to remain focused and continue reaching for excellence. ​”Whether on the podium or through courageous performances in the competition, every member of Team Nigeria has represented our nation with honour, dignity, and pride. ​”On behalf of the Government and the people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, I express profound appreciation to our athletes, coaches, technical officials, medical personnel, administrators, and all those whose dedication and sacrifice made Nigeria’s participation at the Games possible. ​”My administration remains steadfast in its resolve to invest in sports development, strengthen our sporting institutions, improve training facilities, and create greater opportunities for our talented athletes to excel on the continental and global stage,” the President said. items.title: Police arrest three suspects over killing of two officers in Rivers, recover stolen rifles
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor PORT HARCOURT — The Rivers State Police Command says it has arrested three suspects in connection with the killing of two police officers in the state and recovered firearms allegedly stolen during the attack. The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Grace Iringe-Koko Agabe, described the arrests as a major breakthrough in the investigation, saying the operation followed a directive by the Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adewole Adepoju, to track down those responsible. According to Agabe, the officers were attacked on June 29, 2026, while conducting a stop-and-search operation within the Aluu Division. She said two officers lost their lives in the incident, while their service AK-47 rifles were taken by the attackers. She added that the Commissioner of Police immediately ordered the deployment of the Command’s operational and intelligence assets to arrest the suspects and recover the stolen weapons. “Acting on the Commissioner’s directive, operatives of the Command’s Violence Crime Response Unit (VCRU), through credible intelligence and sustained tactical operations, arrested three suspected members of the gang,” she said. The suspects were identified by the police as Maduabuchi Emeka, alias “Doctor,” 34; Chinedu Owhor, 42; and Kamachi Joe, 28, all from Omoku area of Rivers State. According to the police, exhibits recovered include three AK-47 rifles and one Scorpion rifle. The Command also said one of the suspects had allegedly provided information linking the group to other murder cases currently under investigation. Police said efforts were ongoing to apprehend another suspect who remains at large. Agabe said the arrests underscore the Command’s determination to ensure that those responsible for attacks on security personnel and other violent crimes are brought to justice. The police added that investigations are continuing. The post Police arrest three suspects over killing of two officers in Rivers, recover stolen rifles appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: BBNaija 11: Abi mulls exit, cites isolation in house
items.description: By Mary Agbabiaka BBNaija Season 11 contestant, Abi, has expressed a desire to leave the reality show, alleging that she has become the target of hostility from some of her fellow housemates. Her comments followed growing tension in the house after she was nominated for possible eviction, with the housemate claiming she no longer feels comfortable in the competition. Abi made the remarks after the latest nomination process while speaking with fellow contestants, Temi and Nomy, who tried to convince her not to abandon the show despite her frustrations. “I feel like they’re all against me,” Abi said. “Some of them don’t like me, and I can see it in the way they treat me.” In response, Nomy advised her not to allow the actions of other contestants to determine her fate in the competition, urging her to remain focused and continue fighting for her place in the house. Temi also appealed to Abi to rethink her decision, stressing the importance of taking care of her emotional well-being rather than making an impulsive choice. “Don’t let anyone push you into leaving. I think you should check in with your mental health first before making that decision,” Temi said. As of the time of filing this report, Abi had not confirmed whether she would proceed with a voluntary exit or remain in the competition. A total of 19 housemates, including Abi are facing possible eviction this week. Meanwhile, Tram, Barry and Goddessa escaped the eviction list after being saved by fellow contestants, while Chimsom Chuka secured immunity after being saved by the Head of House, guaranteeing all four a place in the third week of the show. items.title: 2027: Uzodimma to inaugurate RHA Diaspora Youth Directorate coordinators in Toronto
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 elections, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Director-General of Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), will lead RHA directors and other leaders to the official inauguration of the organization’s Diaspora Arise platform and the coordinators of its Diaspora Youth Directorate in Toronto, Canada. The event, coordinated by the Directorate of Youth of Renewed Hope Ambassadors, is scheduled to hold on Monday, 10 August 2026 at the Ontario Investment and Trade Centre in Toronto, Canada. A statement by Dr. Mustapha Abdullahi, Director of Youth, RHA and Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria, explained that the inauguration of RHA’s Diaspora Youth coordinators underscores the growing global support for President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda. It further highlights the commitment of Nigerians abroad to national development and to President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. According to Dr. Abdullahi, “The RHA Diaspora Youth platform comes as a strategic vehicle for mobilising young Nigerians across the world to contribute to nation-building, youth leadership, civic engagement and economic transformation. “It also represents a strong affirmation that Nigerians in the diaspora remain critical stakeholders in the success of President Tinubu’s vision for a more prosperous and globally competitive nation.” He said the mobilisation of diaspora youths aligns with the President’s commitment to harnessing the nation’s human capital for sustainable development and national progress. “This initiative is therefore anchored on RHA’s belief that Nigeria’s greatest strength lies in the resilience, innovation and entrepreneurial spirit of its people,” he added. He said Nigerians abroad have continued to distinguish themselves in business, technology, medicine, academia, public service and other sectors across the world. “This inauguration therefore signposts RHA’s expanding reach and reflects a collective determination to build a global network of Nigerians dedicated to promoting good governance, youth empowerment, national unity and economic growth,” he said. He also said that upon their inauguration, the coordinators would be equipped with skills and mobilisation materials, including personalized recruitment codes, QR-enabled registration links, digital mobilisation toolkits and performance-monitoring dashboards to ensure massive mobilisation. Part of the measurable performance targets includes recruiting no fewer than 50 verified members within their first 30 days in office. “The Youth Directorate of RHA remains committed to excellence, integrity and service in our strategic coordination and inclusive leadership, which has continued to inspire and deepen youth participation in national affairs in line with President Tinubu’s vision of a stronger, more prosperous and globally respected Nigeria,” Dr. Abdullahi declared. “We thank Nigerian youths at home and in the diaspora for their unwavering support for the Tinubu administration and urge them to remain focused, united and to continue to work hard for Nigeria’s development aspirations in line with the objectives of the Renewed Hope agenda for the benefit of all citizens,” he concluded. items.title: Missing Uganda opposition aide appears in video after a year
items.description: A video has emerged of an emaciated former aide to one of Uganda’s leading opposition figures months after he vanished, with his family and activists on Tuesday alleging state involvement. Sam Mugumya, 47, was a prominent aide to opposition politician Kizza Besigye — abducted in Kenya two years ago, and currently hospitalised awaiting trial — and was running as a candidate for Besigye’s party. But in August 2025 local media reported Mugumya had been taken by men linked to the security forces, and nothing was heard from him until late July when a video of him, visibly emaciated and seated next to a walker, circulated on social media. The video surfaced as international observers have expressed concerns about a growing crackdown on opposition figures and activists. “I only saw video showing him destroyed and bony,” his mother, Edinansi Katungwesi, told AFP by telephone, confirming his identity. “Since he was kidnapped months ago, I don’t know anything about him or what is happening to him,” she said, adding: “It is the government that took my son and I am so angry at them.” “The government is meant to protect us and has turned against us, and worse of all against my son.” AFP has not been able to verify who recorded the video, when it was shot, or where it was filmed. The army declined to comment when contacted, but a source directed AFP to previous remarks by the defence ministry which in September 2025 denied that Mugumya was in custody. Activist Agather Atuhaire told AFP she believed it was Mugumya, describing his situation as “appalling and shocking”. “I think the military is responsible for his disappearance, detention incommunicado,” she said. “I am so angry and alarmed that we are letting impunity in our country get worse and worse,” she added. The Uganda Law Society has filed a petition for his release. “If he’s being suspected of committing an offence, let him be produced in court and answer the charges,” society vice-president Anthony Asiimwe said. “We cannot continue allowing this kind of lawlessness to take place in this country,” he said. Uganda re-elected President Yoweri Museveni for the seventh time in January, and activists and opposition politicians have warned of an increasingly hostile environment. str-jf/rbu/rh The post Missing Uganda opposition aide appears in video after a year appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Video: Oba Femi makes agbada entrance on RAW after SummerSlam triumph
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian WWE superstar Oba Femi made a bold cultural statement on Monday Night RAW, stepping into the arena in a white agbada just days after defeating wrestling icon Brock Lesnar at SummerSlam. The traditional Yoruba attire drew cheers from fans as the reigning King of the Ring made his entrance, proudly showcasing his Nigerian heritage on one of WWE’s biggest global platforms. Oba Femi’s appearance came after his hard-fought victory over Lesnar in a Hell in a Cell match at SummerSlam in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The clash marked the third meeting between both wrestlers in three months and handed the Nigerian his second win over the WWE legend. Despite enduring a relentless assault, including two crushing blows with steel steps, Oba Femi survived every attack before sealing a memorable victory that further established him as one of WWE’s fastest-rising stars. The emotional conclusion to the match saw Lesnar shake hands with Oba, embrace him and raise his hand before declaring that he was now “the future,” earning loud applause from the crowd. During his RAW appearance, Oba Femi addressed fans in his Nigerian accent while dressed in the flowing agbada, expressing respect for Lesnar and saying the path ahead was now clearer after overcoming one of the sport’s greatest competitors. The 28-year-old, whose real name is Isaac Odugbesan, has become one of WWE’s standout performers, winning around 90 per cent of his matches since joining the promotion. Oba Femi’s cultural display also fulfilled a promise he made during an earlier interview with CNN’s Larry Madowo, where he vowed to continue promoting Yoruba culture after his SummerSlam showdown with Lesnar. Now holding the King of the Ring crown, Oba Femi has earned the right to challenge for either of WWE’s world championships, with fans eagerly awaiting his next move. items.title: Mahama calls transatlantic slave trade humanity’s gravest crime, urges reparatory justice during Jamaica visit
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has described the transatlantic slave trade and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans as “the gravest crime committed against humanity”, urging the international community to confront the legacy of slavery through historical truth, justice and accountability. Addressing the Jamaican Parliament during his state visit to Jamaica on Tuesday, August 4, President Mahama said acknowledging the past was essential to building a future based on justice, respect and equality. “As we honour our shared past, we must also confront it with honesty and fairness. History cannot be changed, but it can be acknowledged. And only by acknowledging it can we build a future that is founded on inspiration, justice and respect,” he said. Mahama referenced what he described as a recent United Nations declaration that the transatlantic slave trade and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans constituted “the gravest crime committed to humanity”, arguing that the effects of slavery continue to shape global inequalities long after its formal abolition. “As was recently announced by the United Nations, the Transatlantic slave trade and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans was the gravest crime committed to humanity. The consequences of this grave crime did not end when it was abolished. The consequences continue to shape the patterns of inequality and the conditions that have motivated our children and our wealth,” he said. President Mahama said the pursuit of reparatory justice remained necessary because the historical injustices of slavery continued to have lasting social and economic consequences. “For this reason, we must make steadfast advances in the cause. They should be inspired by our commitment to accountability, recognition of our rights, the recognition of historical wrongs, acknowledgement of the enduring consequences, and a collective determination to build a more just and equitable global order.” Mahama used the occasion to thank Jamaica for supporting Ghana’s reparatory justice efforts at the United Nations, saying the partnership between the two countries had strengthened international advocacy on the issue. “Permit me to express Ghana’s profound appreciation to the government and people of Jamaica for your unwavering support of Ghana’s initiative at the United Nations, which culminated in the adoption of Resolution A/RES/79/193, and for your invaluable contribution to the Accra Next Steps Conference on Reparatory Justice.” He said Ghana and Jamaica were working together to ensure that descendants of enslaved Africans were recognised and included in shaping a fairer global future. “Together, our two nations are ensuring that the descendants of those who suffered history’s greatest injustices are neither forgotten nor denied a voice in shaping a fairer world.” According to Mahama, the campaign for reparatory justice was ultimately about creating hope for future generations. “Our advocacy is ultimately about hope. Hope that our future generations will inherit a world in which historical truth is acknowledged, human dignity is upheld, and justice becomes the foundation for a lasting and free civilisation. That is the vision that continues to unite us. It is a vision to which we remain unwaveringly committed.” The President also stressed that the history of people of African descent should not be viewed solely through the lens of oppression, but also through their resilience and contributions to global civilisation. “The story of people of African descent is not simply one of suffering. It is a story of resilience, excellence and enduring achievement. It is a story of civilisations that advanced humanity, of people who fought tirelessly for justice, of innovators who expanded the frontiers of science and technology, of artists whose creativity enriched global culture, and of statesmen and women who inspired nations to believe in the possibilities of freedom and self-determination.”

items.title: L’Afrique participera à la mission lunaire chinoise Chang’e 8 prévu en 2029
items.description: AFRIQUE-CHINE-ESPACE-LUNE-COOPERATION L’Afrique participera à la mission lunaire chinoise Chang’e 8 prévu en 2029 Ouagadougou, 4 août 2026 (AIB)- Des pays africains prévoient de participer à la mission chinoise d’exploration lunaire Chang’e 8, à travers l’African Space Initiative, dans le cadre d’une coopération fondée sur « l’ouverture et l’inclusivité », a rapporté le journal chinois Global Times. « L’African Space Initiative prévoit de participer à la mission lunaire chinoise Chang’e 8, sur des principes d’ouverture et d’inclusivité », a déclaré Carla Mitchell, directrice de la mission Africa2Moon et responsable du programme Afrique de l’Observatoire sud-africain de radioastronomie (SARAO). Selon la chercheuse, cette coopération avec la Chine représente une étape historique pour l’Afrique, qui pourra ainsi démontrer ses avancées dans le domaine aérospatial. « Pour la première fois, des institutions africaines apporteront leur propre instrument scientifique à une mission d’exploration lunaire, au lieu de participer uniquement par le biais de collaborations de recherche basées sur Terre », a-t-elle souligné, ajoutant que l’importance de cette initiative dépasse largement la surface lunaire. Carla Mitchell a indiqué que cette collaboration permettra à l’Afrique de renforcer ses capacités en ingénierie, de former des spécialistes hautement qualifiés et de créer de nouvelles opportunités pour les universités et le secteur industriel. « La coopération ne doit jamais être vue comme un pays qui en aide un autre. Elle doit plutôt être envisagée comme une multitude de nations unissant leurs forces pour atteindre des objectifs qu’aucune ne pourrait réaliser seule », a-t-elle précisé. La responsable du programme Afrique de SARAO a également rappelé la vision portée par Africa2Moon : « Notre mission n’est pas simplement d’atteindre la Lune, mais de faire en sorte que chaque jeune Africain croie qu’il a sa place dans l’avenir de l’humanité parmi les étoiles ». Prévue pour 2029, la mission lunaire Chang’e 8 regroupera des instruments scientifiques provenant de onze pays. Elle constituera une étape préparatoire au déploiement de la Station internationale de recherche lunaire. Agence d’information du Burkina Tass Attention photo d’illustration

items.title: Ukraine: « Très peu » d’Ukrainiens soutiennent encore Zelenski, selon son ex-porte-parole
items.description: Ukraine: « Très peu » d’Ukrainiens soutiennent encore Zelenski, selon son ex-porte-parole Ouagadougou, 4 août 2026 (AIB)- L’ancienne porte-parole du président ukrainien Vladimir Zelenski, Ioulia Mendel, a affirmé que le chef de l’État ukrainien ne bénéficie plus que d’un soutien « extrêmement faible » dans son pays, provenant uniquement de personnes qui tirent profit du système existant, dans un entretien accordé à un journal. « Très peu d’Ukrainiens soutiennent Zelenski. Ceux qui le soutiennent encore travaillent souvent pour le gouvernement ou profitent directement du système », a déclaré Ioulia Mendel. Selon elle, plusieurs de ses connaissances estiment que l’Ukraine s’est transformée sous la direction de Vladimir Zelenski en une autocratie. Elle a également indiqué que la confiance de la population envers les autorités s’est ébranlée et que les militaires manquent de motivation. « L’État accuse ceux qui fuient le pays et le peuple accuse l’État : c’est une déloyauté réciproque », a-t-elle déclaré. Ioulia Mendel a par ailleurs affirmé que plusieurs personnes pensaient que Vladimir Zelenski n’achèverait pas son premier mandat en raison de son manque de professionnalisme. « Il s’était brouillé avec l’administration [américaine de Joe] Biden, avec des diplomates américains, ses relations avec [la chancelière allemande Angela] Merkel étaient exécrables », a-t-elle soutenu. items.title: CIHRM Ghana confers chartered status on 35 HR professionals, admits 182 Associate Members
items.description: The Chartered Institute of Human Resource Management, Ghana (CIHRM Ghana) has conferred Chartered Human Resource Management Practitioner status on 35 professionals and admitted 182 new Associate Members at its 16th Conferral and 20th Graduation Ceremony. The ceremony, held at the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) in Accra, under the theme, “ Building Future-Fit HR Practitioners to Drive Business Sustainability ,” highlighted the growing importance of strategic, ethical and technologically competent HR professionals in building sustainable organisations and supporting Ghana’s development. With the addition of the new members, the Institute’s Chartered membership increased from 452 in November 2025 to 487, while its Associate membership rose from 2,686 to 2,868. In his welcome address, the Chief Executive Officer of CIHRM Ghana, Dr. Francis Eduku, congratulated the graduands and conferees for demonstrating resilience, discipline and commitment throughout their professional certification journey. “Today, we celebrate not only your remarkable achievements but also your resilience, discipline and strength of character,” he said. Dr. Eduku noted that the rapidly changing world of work requires HR professionals to embrace continuous learning and remain responsive to emerging developments. “Knowledge and skills we acquire today may not be relevant tomorrow. We must therefore strive to become lifelong learners and be intentionally inquisitive about what is happening inside and outside our organisations,” he stated. He stressed that future-fit HR practitioners must be proactive and capable of preparing organisations for emerging opportunities and potential disruptions. “Future-fit HR practitioners must be anticipatory, nimble and agile in their HR delivery. They must not only focus on what is happening but also prioritise what could happen,” he added. The CEO further urged the new members to uphold professional ethics and integrity, charging them to be HR professionals who “choose principle over popularity, fairness over favouritism and courage over silence,” and, above all, “choose integrity when no one is watching.” Delivering the keynote address, Professor Obi Berko Damoah, Head of the Department of Organisation and Human Resource Management at the University of Ghana Business School, described the ceremony as a celebration of excellence, professionalism and a commitment to Ghana’s future. “The future of organisations will not be determined by technology alone, nor by financial capital alone. It will be determined by the quality of people who are prepared to harness technology ethically, strategically and sustainably,” he said. Professor Damoah explained that being future-fit extends beyond the ability to use artificial intelligence and other digital technologies. It requires the mindset, competencies, agility and leadership capacity to anticipate change rather than merely react to it. He urged HR professionals to move beyond traditional administrative roles and become strategic partners in leading organisational transformation. “Future-fit professionals do not wait for disruption before responding. They prepare organisations before disruption occurs. They do not simply solve today’s problems; they build the organisational capabilities required to address tomorrow’s challenges,” he stated. He identified eight competencies that would distinguish outstanding HR professionals in the coming decade: strategic thinking; digital and artificial intelligence literacy; emotional intelligence; data-driven decision-making; sustainability and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) orientation; change leadership; ethical leadership and governance; and lifelong learning and adaptability. Professor Damoah emphasised that, while technology is transforming the workplace, human qualities such as empathy, trust, relationship-building and ethical judgment will remain essential. “The future belongs to HR professionals who are digitally confident yet deeply human,” he said. He also encouraged the newly admitted members to focus on making meaningful contributions to their organisations and society. “Do not aspire merely to occupy positions. Aspire to create impact. Do not seek only promotions. Seek significance,” he urged. The Chairperson of the Professional Certification Board (PCB) and Head of HR at Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) Mrs. Anita Andrews Nanfuri, congratulated the new Associate and Chartered Members and encouraged them to continue building on the knowledge and skills acquired through the professional certification programme. Mrs. Nanfuri also announced significant growth in enrolment for the Institute’s professional certification programme, with more than 200 students registered to sit for Level One examinations—representing a 300 per cent increase over the previous year. The growth was largely attributed to a special arrangement with the Institute of Professional Studies of the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), which has been permitted to run Level One of the CIHRM Ghana Professional Certification Programme as part of its Access Course. The newly admitted Associate Members were encouraged to progress to Level Four, while the newly Chartered Members were urged to aspire to Fellowship and contribute actively to the growth of the Institute and the HR profession. The Chartered Institute of Human Resource Management, Ghana is the legally mandated professional body established under the Chartered Institute of Human Resource Management, Ghana Act, 2020 (Act 1020), to regulate the practice of human resource management and set professional standards for HR practitioners in Ghana.

items.title: MBF backs Onaiyekan, CBCN, urges Tinubu to heed concerns on hardship
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) has declared its support for the Archbishop Emeritus of the Catholic Archdiocese of Abuja, Cardinal John Onaiyekan, and the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN), following criticism of the cleric over comments on the country’s economic and security challenges. In a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Spokesman, Luka Binniyat, the socio-cultural organisation described the criticism of Cardinal Onaiyekan by some presidential aides as “unfair, unnecessary and completely misplaced.” The forum urged the Federal Government to reflect on the observations made by the Catholic bishops rather than dismissing them. Cardinal Onaiyekan had, after a meeting between President Bola Tinubu and members of the CBCN, said the President appeared not to be receiving accurate information about the conditions facing ordinary Nigerians. Responding, the MBF said the Cardinal spoke in the public interest and reflected the experiences of many Nigerians. “The Middle Belt Forum expresses its total solidarity with His Eminence, John Cardinal Onaiyekan, on his position regarding poverty and hardship in Nigeria,” the statement said. According to the group, the Cardinal’s remarks should not be viewed through a political lens but as contributions to national discourse by a respected religious leader. The MBF also called on President Tinubu to undertake an independent assessment of the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians, particularly victims of terrorism and violent attacks. It urged the President to engage directly with displaced persons, farmers, widows, market women, unemployed youths and community leaders to gain firsthand insight into the challenges they face. The forum said communities in the Middle Belt had endured years of insecurity, with many residents displaced by violent attacks, leading to the destruction of homes, farmlands and livelihoods. While acknowledging the efforts and sacrifices of the military and other security agencies, the MBF maintained that insecurity continues to affect farming, business activities and the daily lives of millions of Nigerians. On the economy, the forum argued that although the national minimum wage had increased, rising inflation and the depreciation of the naira had reduced workers’ purchasing power, making it more difficult for many households to meet basic needs. It also cited increases in the cost of fuel, food, transportation, electricity, cooking gas, healthcare and education as factors contributing to the hardship experienced by many Nigerians. The MBF urged the President to welcome constructive criticism and engage with differing views as part of efforts to address the country’s challenges. It reiterated its support for the CBCN and Cardinal Onaiyekan, saying discussions on poverty, insecurity and the welfare of citizens are legitimate contributions to national development. items.title: Education Ministry urges calm over BECE results, says action will depend on Chief Examiner’s report
items.description: The Ministry of Education has urged stakeholders to remain calm over concerns about the credibility of the 2026 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) results, stating that any decision on the matter will be guided by the Chief Examiner’s report. The response follows allegations by the Ghana National Association of Private Schools (GNAPS) that some candidates received grades that did not reflect their performance, with claims that a number of students were even awarded results in subjects they neither registered for nor sat. Responding to the concernson JoyNews, the Ministry’s spokesperson, Hashim Mohammad, said the government would not rush to conclusions before receiving the official report from the Chief Examiner. “I would not entirely dismiss the allegations. However, it is important that after every examination, we wait for the Chief Examiner’s report. It is only after receiving that report that we can make a meaningful analysis of the results,” he said. Mr. Mohammad noted that examination scripts are marked anonymously, making it difficult to immediately conclude that any group of candidates was deliberately discriminated against. “When examiners are marking answer booklets, the scripts do not indicate who the student is. So it is difficult to suggest that any child has been deliberately discriminated against,” he explained. He appealed to parents, school operators and other stakeholders to exercise patience while the post-examination review process is completed. “I want to calm them down and advise them to wait for the Chief Examiner’s report,” he said. “If the report or subsequent findings establish grounds for concern, the Honourable Minister will not hesitate to direct the Ghana Education Service, if necessary, to set up a committee to investigate the complaints,” he said. While acknowledging that concerns have been raised, the Ministry maintained that it would await the official report before determining whether further action is required.

items.title: End of Monday Sit-at-Home? Soludo hails return of traffic in Onitsha
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has expressed delight after encountering heavy traffic in the commercial city of Onitsha on Monday, describing it as a sign that the long-standing Monday sit-at-home has eased significantly. The governor, who attended the Delta State Economic Summit in Asaba, apologised for arriving about 15 minutes late, explaining that he was delayed by traffic in Onitsha. “Today is Monday, and experiencing traffic in Onitsha on a Monday can only mean one thing: the Monday sit-at-home is over,” Soludo said. Earlier this year, the Anambra State Government reiterated that there was no official Monday sit-at-home order in the state and warned that traders and transport operators who shut their businesses on Mondays without lawful justification could face sanctions. Speaking at the summit, Soludo said the improvement in commercial activities reflected the positive impact of his administration’s efforts to restore normal economic life across the state. The governor also urged Nigerians to prioritise locally made products, arguing that doing so would stimulate economic growth, create jobs and support local industries. “We cannot create the jobs we desire if we continue patronising foreign and imported goods,” he said. Soludo said he had adopted Akwete fabric as his preferred attire after being introduced to it by his daughter in 2019, adding that the decision had helped improve the livelihoods of women weavers in the community. He also referenced the recent announcement of a N2 billion donation to the Akwete community to expand production, noting that increased patronage of locally produced goods would further strengthen the economy. “If all 247 million Nigerians wear only Made-in-Nigeria goods, more than 10 million jobs will be created. We cannot create the kind of jobs we want if we continue relying on imported products,” he said. The governor called on Nigerians to support indigenous manufacturers by choosing locally made goods, saying such a shift would boost employment, increase incomes and drive sustainable economic development. items.title: 7 countries that recently changed their names
items.description: Countries sometimes change their names to reflect their history, culture, language, political identity or a new national direction. While some changes involve a completely different name, others are adjustments to the way a country’s name is officially written or pronounced internationally. The latest example is Nauru, which has moved to adopt Naoero as its official name. Here are seven countries that have changed their names or adopted new official forms in recent years. 1. Nauru → Naoero Nauru is the latest country to make a major change to its official name. The Pacific island nation has adopted Naoero, its traditional name, replacing Nauru as the country’s official English-language name. The move is intended to better reflect the country’s Indigenous language and cultural identity. The change makes Nauru one of the most recent countries to alter its official national name. 2. Turkey → Türkiye In 2022, the country internationally known as Turkey officially began using Türkiye at the United Nations. The change followed a campaign by the Turkish government to promote the country’s name in its Turkish form. The United Nations formally recognised the change after receiving a letter from the Turkish government. The country is still commonly referred to as Turkey in everyday English, but Türkiye is its official international name. 3. Swaziland → Eswatini The southern African kingdom of Swaziland officially changed its name to Eswatini in 2018. King Mswati III announced the change during celebrations marking the country’s 50th independence anniversary. The monarch said the new name reflected the country’s traditional identity and helped eliminate confusion with Switzerland. Eswatini means “land of the Swazi” in the Swazi language. 4. Macedonia → North Macedonia The country formerly known simply as Macedonia officially became the Republic of North Macedonia in 2019. The change followed the Prespa Agreement between North Macedonia and Greece. The naming dispute had lasted for decades because Greece has a region called Macedonia. The new name helped resolve the dispute and paved the way for North Macedonia’s accession to NATO. 5. Czech Republic → Czechia The Czech Republic adopted Czechia as its short-form name in 2016. The change did not replace the country’s formal name, which remains the Czech Republic. Instead, Czechia became the shorter geographical and political name, similar to how “France” is used instead of “French Republic” in ordinary contexts. 6. Cape Verde → Cabo Verde The West African island nation officially changed the way its name is used internationally from Cape Verde to Cabo Verde. The government requested that the Portuguese name be used without translation. The change reflects the country’s Portuguese heritage and its preference for its native name. 7. East Timor → Timor-Leste East Timor, the English name commonly used for the country, became internationally known as Timor-Leste following its independence in 2002. Timor-Leste is the country’s Portuguese name and is its official name. The Southeast Asian nation restored its independence after a long period of Indonesian occupation and became an independent country in 2002. items.title: Repatriation isn’t an act of kindness, it’s a right – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama has declared that repatriation for people of African descent is a fundamental right rather than an act of charity, calling on African countries to establish legal pathways for members of the global African family to return and settle on the continent. Addressing the Jamaican Parliament on Tuesday, August 4, during his State Visit to the Caribbean nation, President Mahama said the right of return should be recognised across Africa as part of efforts to reconnect the continent with its diaspora. “The rights of persons of African descent in the diaspora to return to the mother continent is not an act of charity or compassion. Repatriation is not an act of kindness,” he said. “Repatriation is a right of all persons of African descent to return to the mother continent and settle or reside if they wish.” President Mahama highlighted Ghana’s efforts to facilitate the return of the African diaspora, noting that the country enacted the Right of Abode Act in 2000 to allow eligible persons of African descent to live permanently in Ghana. He added that the government is also considering a new Homeland Return Bill, which will establish clearer legal pathways for residence and citizenship for members of the global African family seeking to reconnect with their ancestral homeland. According to the President, the proposed legislation forms part of Ghana’s broader commitment to strengthening ties with Africans in the diaspora. President Mahama also revealed that he intends to champion the right of return across the continent if elected Chairperson of the African Union. “This is one of the articles of the manifesto I wish to push when I become the AU Chairman, that all African nations must have a right of return for all members of the global African family,” he said.

items.title: Mahama calls for stronger trade and investment partnerships between Africa-Caribbean
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called for a stronger partnership between Africa and the Caribbean, urging the two regions to transform their shared history into a shared future built on economic cooperation, innovation and coordinated global action. Addressing a special joint sitting of the Jamaican Parliament during his state visit on August 4, President Mahama said the historic ties between Africa and the Caribbean should now serve as a foundation for deeper collaboration that improves the lives of their people. “The challenge before us has never been clearer,” he said. “We must transform our shared history into shared prosperity. We must move beyond sentiment and build partnerships that create opportunities, expand prosperity and improve the lives of our people.” The President invoked the words of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, saying the vision of African unity remains as relevant today as it was during the struggle for independence. “As our first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, reminded us, ‘The forces that unite us are intrinsic and greater than the superimposed influences that keep us apart,'” he said. “Those words speak as powerfully to us today as they did at the dawn of African liberation.” President Mahama said the current generation must focus on achieving economic transformation, scientific advancement and technological progress while ensuring the liberation of the African mind. “It demands confidence in our own institutions. It demands belief in our own capabilities and an unwavering commitment to accountability and excellence,” he said. “Above all, it requires that our young people see themselves not as descendants of slaves, but as heirs to greatness and architects of an even greater future.” Highlighting the opportunities before both regions, the President said Africa’s youthful population, abundant natural resources and growing innovation ecosystem position the continent for rapid development, while Jamaica continues to provide global leadership on climate justice, sustainable development, democracy and multilateral cooperation. He described Jamaica as an important gateway to the Americas and said both regions possess enormous human talent, cultural influence and economic potential. “History has connected us, and the future now calls upon us to work together,” President Mahama said. He called for stronger cooperation between the African Union and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM), as well as closer collaboration within the United Nations and other multilateral institutions. “We must coordinate our positions on issues that will define the future of humanity,” he said. “Whether the challenge is climate change, reform of the international financial architecture, food security, public health or digital transformation, our voices will carry greater weight if we speak together.” President Mahama said the Africa-Caribbean partnership should no longer be defined solely by a shared past but by a shared vision for the future. He also highlighted Ghana’s recently launched Accra Reforms initiative, describing it as a blueprint for reshaping global governance and creating a more equitable international system. “The Accra Reforms reflect our belief that the institutions governing the world must evolve to reflect the realities and aspirations of the 21st century,” he said. According to the President, too many developing countries continue to face structural barriers, including limited access to financing, unfair trading arrangements and inadequate representation in global decision-making bodies. “These inequities cannot define our future,” he said. “The Accra Reforms call for a new development paradigm founded on mutual respect, productive investment and genuine partnership.” President Mahama reiterated Ghana’s call for comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including permanent African representation on the UN Security Council, saying developing countries must participate as equal partners in shaping global solutions.

items.title: Zoundwéogo: L’ONASER mobilise les acteurs régionaux autour de la Nuit des acteurs et partenaires de la sécurité routière
items.description: Burkina-Zoundwéogo-Sécurité-Routière-Échanges Zoundwéogo: L'ONASER mobilise les acteurs régionaux autour de la Nuit des acteurs et partenaires de la sécurité routière Manga, 3 août 2026 (AIB) – L'Office national de la sécurité routière (ONASER) a rencontré, lundi à Manga, les autorités régionales, les acteurs du transport et les professionnels des médias afin de les mobiliser pour l'organisation de la Nuit des acteurs et partenaires de la sécurité routière, une initiative visant à récompenser les meilleures actions en faveur de la prévention des accidents de la circulation et de la promotion du civisme routier. Cette rencontre s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une tournée régionale entreprise par l'ONASER pour fédérer les différents acteurs autour de cet évènement national. Selon le chef du service de l'éducation à la sécurité routière de l'ONASER, Lamoussa Ouango, la démarche vise principalement à organiser, dans chaque région, des appels à projets destinés à susciter des candidatures et à identifier les initiatives citoyennes contribuant à l'amélioration de la sécurité routière. « Il s'agit d'encourager les bonnes pratiques et de mettre en lumière les personnes, associations ou structures qui œuvrent quotidiennement à la prévention des accidents et à la promotion des comportements responsables sur nos routes », a-t-il expliqué. Abordant l'organisation pratique, M. Ouango a indiqué que l'ONASER entend mobiliser les Forces de défense et de sécurité, les services techniques en charge des transports et de la mobilité ainsi que les médias afin d'assurer le lancement, le suivi et la sélection des meilleurs projets au niveau régional. Les lauréats retenus dans chaque région seront récompensés lors de la Nuit des acteurs et partenaires de la sécurité routière, dont la date de tenue sera communiquée ultérieurement. Ils recevront des distinctions et seront élevés au rang d'ambassadeurs de la sécurité routière. Le responsable de l'ONASER a enfin insisté sur le rôle des médias dans la réussite de l'initiative, estimant qu'ils ont pour mission « d'informer, de sensibiliser et de promouvoir les bonnes pratiques en matière de sécurité routière ». Agence d’information du Burkina SM/BGB/bak

items.title: Un glissement de terrain fait 14 morts dans un monastère
items.description: Un glissement de terrain provoqué par de fortes pluies a coûté la vie à 14 pèlerins dans un monastère orthodoxe de la région de l'Amhara, dans le nord de l'Éthiopie. L'information, rapportée, ce mardi 4 août 2026, par plusieurs médias citant un responsable du diocèse, intervient alors que le pays est confronté à de violentes intempéries liées à la saison des pluies. L'Éthiopie est, une nouvelle fois, endeuillée par une catastrophe naturelle, après les inondations et les glissements de terrain survenus en mars dernier et qui avaient coûté la vie à 80 personnes dans le nord du pays. Selon des médias citant un responsable du diocèse, un glissement de terrain survenu lundi 3 août 2026 dans la localité de Sela Dingay, située à environ 200 kilomètres au nord-est d'Addis-Abeba, a fait 14 morts et cinq blessés. Le drame s'est produit dans le monastère orthodoxe Tsadkane Mariam, où de nombreux fidèles étaient réunis pour des prières. Les fortes précipitations enregistrées dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi auraient fragilisé le terrain. Le responsable du diocèse, Megabe Hadis Neka Tibeb Ababu, a expliqué que le phénomène «s'est produit lundi à sept heures du matin, après des pluies très abondantes pendant la nuit, accompagnées d'éclairs et de tonnerre». Selon son témoignage, une importante coulée de boue mêlée à des rochers a dévalé la colline dominant le site religieux, ensevelissant une partie du monastère et les pèlerins qui s'y trouvaient. Le responsable religieux a précisé que «quatorze fidèles qui priaient dans le monastère ont été tués sur le coup. Trois personnes gravement blessées ont été transportées à l'hôpital», avant d'ajouter que le bilan était «définitif». Dans un premier temps, les autorités locales de la zone de Shewa-Nord avaient confirmé la mort de 14 personnes, évoquant un «séisme et un glissement de terrain soudain», sans fournir davantage de précisions sur les circonstances du drame. Avec près de 130 millions d'habitants, l'Éthiopie traverse actuellement sa longue saison des pluies, qui s'étend généralement de juin à septembre dans une grande partie du pays. Cette période est régulièrement marquée par des catastrophes naturelles, notamment dans les zones rurales où vivent plus des trois quarts de la population. Ce nouveau drame rappelle la vulnérabilité de l'Éthiopie face aux aléas climatiques. En juillet 2024, un glissement de terrain dans le sud du pays avait fait au moins 257 morts. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un glissement de terrain fait 14 morts dans un monastère est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: CBN holds fair in Gombe to deepen financial inclusion, promote economic growth
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Gombe Branch, on Tuesday organised a stakeholders’ fair to promote financial inclusion, enhance public awareness of the Bank’s operations and obtain feedback on its policies and services. The event, held at the International Conference Centre in Gombe, brought together government officials, financial sector stakeholders, business operators, students and members of the public. Speaking at the opening ceremony, the CBN Branch Controller, Alhaji Yunusa Buba Mubi, said the fair was designed to strengthen engagement between the apex bank and the public through sensitisation, education and interactive feedback. Mubi disclosed that a delegation from the CBN headquarters, led by the Acting Director of the Corporate Communications and Investors Relations Department, was in Gombe for the sensitisation programme. He urged participants to pay close attention to the presentations, ask relevant questions and provide constructive feedback to help the Bank improve its operations and services. According to him, the initiative is part of the CBN’s strategic efforts to deepen financial inclusion, stimulate economic growth and ensure its policies and services effectively reach grassroots communities across the country. Representing the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Mrs. Hakama Sidi Ali said the fair was one of the Bank’s strategic initiatives aimed at improving the lives and livelihoods of Nigerians through enhanced financial literacy and greater access to alternative payment channels. She said the CBN remains committed to maintaining monetary and financial system stability, controlling inflation and ensuring price stability in line with its statutory mandate, noting that these objectives are critical to sustainable economic development. Also speaking, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, represented by the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government, Alhaji Salihu Adamu Sambo, commended the CBN for expanding digital financial services, saying the initiative has made business transactions easier, faster and more convenient for individuals and businesses. He, however, cautioned Nigerians against cybercrime and other fraudulent activities capable of undermining confidence in the nation’s financial system and slowing economic growth. The fair featured presentations and interactive sessions on the theme, “Driving Alternative Payment Channels as Tools for Financial Inclusion, Growth and Accelerated Economic Development.” Participants highlighted the importance of digital payment systems as key drivers of inclusive growth, innovation and national economic transformation. items.title: 144 children lost to diphtheria, measles since January in Karachi
items.description: • Deaths from vaccine-preventable diseases reported at four tertiary care city hospitals • Expert says most parents fail to ensure children receive recommended doses on time • EPI official claims cases declined this year KARACHI: At least 144 children have lost their lives to measles and diphtheria — both vaccine-preventable infections — at four key tertiary care hospitals in the first seven months of this year, it emerged on Monday. Sources said that a total of 1,915 cases of measles with 125 mortalities have been reported at the four hospitals —Indus Hospital (IH), Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC), National Institute of Child Health (NICH) and Sindh Institute of Child Health and Neonatology (SICHN) — this year so far. Eighty-one cases of diphtheria were reported at SIDH&RC, eight at Indus Hospital (8) with 19 deaths. Detailed analysis of the data showed that at least 17 children have lost their lives to measles — a highly contagious viral infection — at IH with around 850 cases this year so far. In addition, a child died of diphtheria at the hospital, which has recorded at least eight of cases of the bacterial infection. At SID&RC, at least 54 children — 36 from measles and 18 from diphtheria — have died during the period between Jan 1 and July 26, 2026. The total number of measles and diphtheria cases reported at the facility was 575 and 81, respectively. While detailed data of the NICH was not available, sources at the province’s largest public-sector hospital for children shared that at least seven children have died of measles at the facility in recent weeks. “We get complicated cases after the patient has already been mismanaged at multiple health facilities. At that stage, measles has either turned into encephalitis [a dangerous swelling and inflammation of the brain] or pneumonia [the most common measles’ complication]. The former carries a significant risk of death and long-term disability,” a doctor at the NICH told Dawn on the condition of anonymity. Information gathered from SICHN showed that 484 cases of measles have been reported this year so far at the facility with 65 deaths. Role of healthcare providers Explaining why a significant number of children couldn’t get protection against diseases that could easily be prevented through vaccines available free of cost under the Expanded Programme for Immunisation (EPI), Dr Khalid Shafi of the Pakistan Paediatric Association said that the tragedy in Pakistan was that the coverage rate of vaccine doses given at birth was 90 per cent but this number declined sharply as the child grows, requiring subsequent doses of vaccines. “Unfortunately, parents get negligent and the child either gets no or partial protection against several diseases including measles, typhoid and polio,” he said, adding that around 20 to 25 per cent of the child population in the country couldn’t get timely vaccination. He pointed out that the first shot of measles under the EPI programme was given at nine months and the second (the last) one at 15 months. “If 95 per cent of our children get the two shots at the right time, we can easily control this disease as the vaccine provides herd immunity to the rest of the population. Most children in our country, however, either fail to receive any dose or get only partial protection through one dose.” To address this challenge, he said countrywide vaccination drives were launched every four years. Last year, a national level drive was launched for children aged six months to five years, who were given an additional dose of MR (measles and rubella) vaccine. “Along with the government efforts, our healthcare providers have a crucial role to help tackle the vaccination coverage gap. When an ailing child reports to them, they must ask about his or her vaccination history/status and provide proper counselling to parents, if they find any vaccine doses missing. “Having said that, parents have the prime responsibility to protect their child and they must play their part with diligence. Though there are cases with children falling sick despite getting the vaccine shots, their numbers are few and the disease intensity in such cases is mild.” EPI’s response In his response, EPI Project Director Dr Raj Kumar said cases of measles and diphtheria had declined this year in the province, especially measles which saw a 35 per cent drop. According to him, 148 cases of diphtheria with 14 deaths were reported in the province in the first seven months of 2025, while this year so far 10 deaths have been reported with 46 confirmed cases. “Last year, we had 4,626 cases of measles in the first seven months with 57 deaths in the province. This year so far, we have 3,025 cases with 59 deaths,” he said. Highlighting challenges, he said that pockets of unvaccinated children and parental negligence were primary drivers of increase in cases. “Along with that, there are myths surrounding me­­asles and parents prefer traditional remedies, keep their child at home, resulting in disease complications,” he explained, adding that the government had run vaccination campaigns to cover missed children and planning to continue this process and that an additional 970 vaccinators had been recruited to address HR shortages. The government had surveillance units and collected data from hospitals, he said. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Renard returns for second spell as Ivory Coast coach
items.description: Herve Renard, who led Ivory Coast to 2015 Africa Cup of Nations glory, has returned for a second spell as coach, the Ivorian football federation (FIF) announced on Tuesday. The 57-year-old Frenchman replaces Emerse Fae, who was not retained despite guiding The Elephants to the AFCON title in 2024. Fae also took the Ivorians into the knockout stage of the World Cup for the first time in June, losing 2-1 to Norway in the last 32. Renard had the thankless task of being hired as Tunisia coach after they lost their opening World Cup group match 5-1 to Sweden, before overseeing two more heavy defeats by Japan and the Netherlands. He has plenty of experience in African football and also coached Zambia to an emotional triumph in the Africa Cup of Nations in 2012. Renard has also had spells at Morocco, Ghana and Angola. He was in charge of Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup where they beat eventual champions Argentina in the group stage. Renard took charge of the Saudis again in 2024 but was fired before this year’s World Cup. His first task back with Ivory Coast will be their opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Ghana in September. The finals are being co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. items.title: Zoundwéogo/Entrepreneuriat: 30 jeunes formés en entrepreneuriat rural à Gogo
items.description: Zoundwéogo/Entrepreneuriat: 30 jeunes formés en entrepreneuriat rural à Gogo Gogo, 30 juil. 2026 (AIB) – Trente jeunes de la commune de Gogo ont achevé, jeudi, une session de formation de quatre jours en entrepreneuriat rural, à l'initiative du ministère en charge de la Jeunesse, à travers le Secrétariat permanent de YouthConnekt Burkina, en vue de renforcer leurs capacités en création et en gestion d'activités génératrices de revenus. La cérémonie de clôture, a été présidée par le Président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS), de la commune de Gogo Issa Tiendrébéogo, en présence du Secrétaire général de la mairie, Karim Dao, des Référents Opportunité-Insertion (ROPI) Paul Kaboré et Ali Gansoré, des formateurs et des bénéficiaires. Mise en œuvre en collaboration avec la Direction régionale en charge de la Jeunesse et la mairie de Gogo, à travers le Service de promotion de l'insertion professionnelle des jeunes (SPIPJ), cette formation visait à doter les participants d'outils pratiques pour développer des initiatives entrepreneuriales en milieu rural. Dans son allocution, le PDS a remercié le ministère en charge de la Jeunesse pour avoir retenu la commune de Gogo parmi les localités bénéficiaires de cette initiative. Il a également salué l'engagement du superviseur et des formateurs pour la qualité des enseignements dispensés. S'adressant aux bénéficiaires, M. Tiendrébéogo les a félicités pour leur discipline, leur assiduité et leur ponctualité tout au long de la session. Il les a invités à mettre en application les connaissances acquises afin d'améliorer leurs activités économiques, avant de réaffirmer la disponibilité de la Délégation spéciale à accompagner les jeunes entrepreneurs de la commune. Le superviseur de la formation, Zakaria Kiendéga, conseiller en emploi, a, pour sa part, remercié les autorités communales pour leur accompagnement ayant permis le bon déroulement de la session. Selon lui, ce renforcement des capacités constitue une opportunité de promouvoir l'entrepreneuriat et l'autonomisation économique des jeunes. Les formateurs, Ami Pamtaba, conseillère de jeunesse et d'éducation permanente au Secrétariat permanent de YouthConnekt Burkina, et Titinga Zoungrana, conseiller de jeunesse, ont indiqué que la formation a porté sur l'esprit d'entreprise, la création d'entreprise, les créneaux porteurs, la gestion d'une microentreprise, le financement de l'entreprise rurale ainsi que la création et la gestion des sociétés coopératives. Ils se sont réjouis de l'implication des participants, marquée par des échanges interactifs et un vif intérêt pour les différents modules, estimant que les compétences acquises contribueront à la pérennisation des activités économiques des bénéficiaires. Au nom des participants, Samuel Baga et Isabelle Yaogo ont exprimé leur reconnaissance aux organisateurs. Ils ont plaidé pour un accompagnement de la mairie dans la création de coopératives, un appui en équipements de production et une facilitation de l'accès au financement des projets portés par les jeunes. Agence d’information du Burkina KP/BGB/bak
